Manufacturing models

## Three ways to make your product

### Private label

You commission a manufacturer to produce a formula adapted to your brand, packaged under your name.
Use it when you want a differentiated product without owning a factory. The formula is typically
co-developed and can be licensed exclusively, with the manufacturer retaining process know-how and
you owning the brand and commercial rights.

[Browse private label manufacturers ][42]

### White label

You select an existing product the manufacturer already produces and apply your branding. Use it
when speed and low MOQs matter more than uniqueness. The formula stays with the manufacturer and may
be sold to other brands in parallel, so you carry less development risk but accept that competitors
may shelve a near-identical product.

[Browse white label manufacturers ][43]

### Contract manufacturing

You hand the manufacturer a complete specification or formula and they produce it to order. Use it
when you have proprietary IP, regulated processes, or volumes that justify dedicated production. You
own the formula, the manufacturer owns the capacity, and the commercial terms are usually structured
around guaranteed minimum runs.

# WELCOME TO WPHA

We are glad you are here and we hope you JOIN US!
Our mission to build collective action to address root-causes and advance public health policy &
practice to achieve a vision for a healthier, safer, and more equitable Wisconsin.
The priorities related to advancing WPHA's mission are to:
* Support the conditions for all people of Wisconsin to be healthy and thrive
* Diversify the membership and leadership of WPHA and support a culture of inclusion and belonging
  where all members can thrive, with special attention to those from historically marginalized
  identities (BIPOC, LGBTQ+)
* Support development and retention of a skilled, resilient, and diverse public health workforce
* Support policy and advocacy that makes Wisconsin the healthiest state for all
* Increase visibility of the value of public health work throughout Wisconsin

## About WPHA

The Wisconsin Public Health Association, Inc. (WPHA) was founded in 1948, and is an affiliate of the
American Public Health Association (APHA). WPHA is a tax-exempt, non-profit with a 501(c)3 status.

## Mission
* (Mission) Build collective action to address root-causes and advance public health policy &
  practice.
* (Vision) A healthier, safer, and more equitable Wisconsin.

[Receive current news, advocacy updates & action alerts, networking resources, upcoming public
health events.][58]

### Follow us on Social Media!

Stay up to date with the most recent news in WPHA and new and exciting updates from us!

> [Wisconsin Public Health Association][59]

## Health Equity in WPHA

WPHA recommends starting with Health Equity Training Modules (created by Mobilizing Action Toward
Community Health (MATCH) and the Wisconsin Center for Public Health Education and Training's
(WiCPHET)). These modules help transition planning processes to better focus on social determinants
of health. The modules' training objectives include: using a broad definition of health that
includes social determinants, reflecting on how conditions of power shape social determinants and
health inequities, and identifying opportunities to operationalize strategies to advance health
equity in practice. MATCH's Health Equity Practice Initiatives website is another resource to learn
more.

The City of Madison's Racial Equity and Social Justice Initiative maintains a comprehensive Racial
Equity and Social Justice Tool process guide, relevant to planning processes, especially policy,
systems, and environmental change (PSE) priorities and objectives.

The Frameworks Institute offers tips to Talk about Health Equity, which may support messaging
development.

The Wisconsin Center for Health Equity offers additional resources, including:
* 2018 Foundational Practices for Health Equity
* 2013 Social, Economic, and Educational Factors that Influence Health
* 2014 Health Disparities and Health Equity Overview

Be a part of an organization in Wisconsin dedicated to advancing statewide public policy change to
eliminate health inequities. We are committed to dismantling systemic racism, reducing poverty, and
integrating health in all policies.
